explain.say: Most airliners cruise between about 10 and 12 kilometres up, higher than Mount Everest. That height is a sweet spot between thin air that is easy to push through and air still thick enough for the wings and engines.

faq.q: Why do planes fly so high?
faq.a: Thin air high up creates much less drag, so a plane flies faster on less fuel. At about 11 kilometres the air is still thick enough for the wings to lift and the engines to breathe.
asks: Why do jets fly at 35,000 feet?
What height do planes fly at?

faq.q: Why is it less bumpy up high?
faq.a: Most clouds, storms and rising warm air are in the lowest part of the atmosphere, below cruising height. Flying above them usually gives a smoother ride, although clear-air turbulence can still happen.
asks: Why is there less turbulence at cruising height?

faq.q: Why don't planes fly even higher?
faq.a: Higher still, the air is so thin that the wings need much more speed to hold the plane up, and the engines can't get enough oxygen. Most airliners have a ceiling of around 12 to 13 kilometres.
asks: What is the highest a plane can fly?

faq.q: Why do planes climb in steps on long flights?
faq.a: As a plane burns fuel it gets lighter, so its best height rises. On long flights pilots ask air traffic control to climb in steps to stay near the most efficient height.

faq.q: How cold is it outside at cruising height?
faq.a: Around minus 50 degrees Celsius or colder. The air is thin and freezing, which is why the cabin has to be pressurised and heated.
asks: What is the temperature outside a plane?

facts: In the standard atmosphere, the air at 11 kilometres is about minus 56 degrees Celsius.
Mount Everest is 8,849 metres high, lower than a typical airliner's cruising height.
